name: Atiyah-Hitchin Space
description: A space of four dimensions with no time in it, the moduli space of two slowly moving magnetic monopoles that Michael Atiyah and Nigel Hitchin found in 1985: a smooth solution of Einstein's vacuum equations with Riemannian signature and self dual curvature. It closes on a 2-sphere at its core, and far away it is the self dual Taub-NUT space with a negative mass.
convention: The length $n$ is the space's only parameter. All four coordinates are spatial, so no component carries a factor of $c$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to arc length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Two slow magnetic monopoles that collide head on fly apart at right angles to the line they came in on [atiyahhitchin1988, bachmaier2025]. Nicholas Manton argued in 1982 that monopoles moving slowly follow geodesics in the space of static solutions with several monopoles [manton1982]. For two monopoles of an $SU(2)$ gauge theory, that space has four dimensions once the centre of mass and the overall phase are set aside [weinbergyi2007, tong2005]. Three of them hold the separation of the pair and the fourth their relative phase [tong2005]. Its metric is Riemannian, with signature $(+,+,+,+)$ and no time in it, and geodesics through it approximate the pair's motion at low speeds [gibbonsmanton1986, bachmaier2025].¶Michael Atiyah and Nigel Hitchin determined that metric in 1985 from its symmetry under rotations and its hyperkähler structure, with no explicit solution for two monopoles in hand [tong2005, atiyahhitchin1985]. In four dimensions a hyperkähler metric has self dual curvature, so the space solves Einstein's vacuum equations [hananypioline2000, ghezelbashmann2004]. Each orbit of the rotations is a 3-geometry with lengths $a$, $b$, and $c$ along its three axes, tied together by three equations of first order [tong2005, ghezelbashmann2004]. Atiyah and Hitchin found four smooth solutions with a region far away: Eguchi-Hanson space, flat space, Taub-NUT space, and their own, the one whose three lengths all differ [weinbergyi2007, atiyahhitchin1985trans]. In their words, "monopoles can get converted into dyons", so a pair that meets may part with electric charges as well as magnetic ones [atiyahhitchin1985, gibbonsmanton1995].¶They solved for their space with the complete elliptic integral $K$ of the first kind [hananypioline2000]. Gary Gibbons and Nicholas Manton fixed the radius $r$ in 1986 by $f = -b/r$, where $f^2dr^2$ is the part of the metric across the orbits [gibbonsmanton1986, weinbergyi2007]. Then $r = 2nK(\sin(\beta/2))$ runs from $\pi n$ to infinity as the angle $\beta$ runs from $0$ to $\pi$, with $n$ the length that sets the scale [weinbergyi2007, ghezelbashmann2004]. At $r = \pi n$ the length $a$ falls to zero while $b$ and $-c$ tend to $\pi n$ [ghezelbashmann2004]. Exchanging the two identical monopoles, an identification of the angles, closes the space smoothly there on a 2-sphere of radius $\pi n$ [weinbergyi2007, atiyahhitchin1985trans, ghezelbashmann2004]. A further identification of the relative phase turns the 2-sphere into a real projective plane and leaves the space a loop that cannot be shrunk to a point [weinbergyi2007, seibergwitten1997].¶Far from the core, $a$ and $b$ approach $r\sqrt{1 - 2n/r}$ and $c$ approaches $-2n/\sqrt{1 - 2n/r}$, and the space becomes the self dual Euclidean Taub-NUT space with a negative mass [ghezelbashmann2004, gibbonsmanton1995, hawking1977]. That limit is singular at $r = 2n$, and the corrections that fall off as $e^{-r/n}$, which carry the overlap of the two monopole cores, remove the singularity [tong2005, ghezelbashmann2004]. Shortly after Atiyah and Hitchin found the metric, Manton derived its far form from two well separated dyons treated as point particles with magnetic, electric, and scalar charges [gibbonsmanton1995, manton1985]. Momentum around the circle of the relative phase is electric charge [hananypioline2000]. Taub-NUT space has a symmetry around that circle which the full metric lacks, so dyons far apart keep their charges and two that come close exchange charge as well as momentum [gibbonsmanton1995].¶Gibbons and Manton followed the geodesics in 1986 as classical orbits and as quantum states, the Hamiltonian proportional to the Laplacian of the space [gibbonsmanton1986]. Far apart the motion generalises the Coulomb problem, which they solved exactly, classically and in quantum mechanics, and they found scattering and bound states of the pair [gibbonsmanton1986]. Monopoles that stay in one plane move on a surface of the space that is, far away, a cone with half its angle removed [bachmaier2025]. A geodesic through its rounded tip turns by $\pi$ on the cone, which is $\pi/2$ in space [bachmaier2025]. Maximilian Bachmaier, Gia Dvali, Josef Seitz, and Juan Sebastián Valbuena-Bermúdez evolved the full field equations of two colliding monopoles in 2025 and found the right angle, the energy of the pair spread around a torus as they met [bachmaier2025].¶Nathan Seiberg and Edward Witten found the same space as the moduli space of vacua of a gauge theory in three dimensions with gauge group $SU(2)$ and eight supercharges [seibergwitten1997]. Nick Dorey, Valentin Khoze, Michael Mattis, David Tong, and Stefan Vandoren confirmed that identification in 1997 with a calculation of one instanton [dorey1997]. In M-theory the orientifold plane of type IIA string theory is this space, as Seiberg and Witten concluded [sen1997enhanced, seibergwitten1997]. Ashoke Sen set $N$ Kaluza-Klein monopoles beside it in 1997, the M-theory form of $N$ D6-branes on that plane, and recovered their gauge symmetry $SO(2N)$ [sen1997enhanced]. Up to scale the further quotient is the unique asymptotically locally flat gravitational instanton of type $D_0$, and Bernd Schroers and Michael Singer glued it to $k$ copies of Taub-NUT space to build those of type $D_k$ [schroerssinger2021]. Atiyah, Manton, and Schroers took the simply connected double cover in 2012 as a model of the proton, with Taub-NUT space for the electron and the cover's topological signature, $1$, for the baryon number [atiyahmantonschroers2012].

related.text: Hawking's self dual Taub-NUT instanton is smooth, Ricci flat, and self dual, as this space is. Far from its core this space is that instanton with its mass made negative, singular at $r = 2n$, and corrections that fall off as $e^{-r/n}$ remove the singularity [gibbonsmanton1995, tong2005].

In Atiyah and Hitchin's classification of 1985, Eguchi and Hanson's space is the smooth solution on the branch where the rotations leave the complex structures fixed, and this space is one of those on the branch where they turn them [weinbergyi2007, atiyahmantonschroers2012]. Both close on a 2-sphere.

Taub-NUT continued to Euclidean signature, in its self dual case and with the sign of its mass reversed, is this space far from its core, up to corrections that fall off as $e^{-r/n}$ [gibbonsmanton1995, ghezelbashmann2004].
Euclidean Taub-NUT space with a time added. In M-theory, $N$ of these monopoles set beside this space are $N$ D6-branes on the orientifold plane of type IIA string theory [sen1997enhanced].
